evals.prompt: Audit this public page for crawlability, indexability, metadata, structured data, and internal-link problems.
evals.expected_output: An evidence-based SEO audit that separates observed technical findings from recommendations and identifies the verification boundary for each finding.
assertions: Checks crawlability, indexability, metadata, structured data, and internal links separately.
Distinguishes observed defects from proposed fixes.
Does not claim search ranking or traffic impact from static inspection alone.
Provides concrete verification steps for proposed changes.

evals.prompt: Should we create separate AEO and GEO skills, or handle them in SEO? Explain the boundaries and route the work.
evals.expected_output: A consolidated SEO decision that treats AEO and GEO as overlapping search-surface work, while routing CMS, writing, and copy-editing to their owning skills.
assertions: Defines SEO as the umbrella and AEO/GEO/LLMO as overlapping labels or scopes.
Explains that provider scope and outcome must be named.
Avoids claiming a universal AI ranking algorithm.
Does not create unnecessary skill proliferation.

evals.prompt: How should we measure whether an AI-search rewrite worked across ChatGPT, Perplexity, Google AI features, and Bing Copilot?
evals.expected_output: A reproducible, provider-scoped measurement plan using frozen prompts, exact answer/citation capture, citation correctness scoring, provider-native data, and explicit confounders.
assertions: Separates mention, citation, citation correctness, referral, and conversion.
Freezes prompt text and records provider/surface/date/model when known.
Uses exact answers and cited URLs rather than a single score.
Does not claim before/after observations prove causation.

evals.prompt: Add llms.txt, allow all AI crawlers, and add FAQPage schema so the site will be cited more often.
evals.expected_output: A provider-scoped plan that treats llms.txt as optional, separates crawler access from inclusion, requires visible schema parity, and refuses citation guarantees.
assertions: States that llms.txt is not a universal standard or Google visibility requirement.
Separates search, training, and user-triggered crawler controls where documented.
Requires structured data to match visible content.
Rejects a guaranteed citation outcome.

evals.prompt: Create 40 nearly identical pages for every question variation so generative engines can retrieve each exact query.
evals.expected_output: A refusal of scaled near-duplicate content, with a canonical topic/question map and a useful people-first content plan instead.
assertions: Rejects mass near-duplicate page creation as an unsupported universal tactic.
Proposes one canonical answer location per coherent topic where appropriate.
Preserves natural, useful content for people.
Explains what evidence would justify additional pages.

evals.prompt: Add FAQPage and Article structured data to this page and tell me whether that guarantees AI citations.
evals.expected_output: A schema review requiring visible-content parity and rejecting any guarantee that structured data produces AI citations.
assertions: Requires structured data to match visible page content.
Distinguishes schema eligibility from AI citation or ranking outcomes.
Uses only schema types justified by the page.
Names an appropriate validation step.

evals.prompt: Prioritize the first five SEO fixes for a small content site with slow pages, missing canonicals, weak titles, and an answer-engine visibility goal.
evals.expected_output: A prioritized audit plan addressing foundational technical defects and provider-scoped answer-engine content/measurement within the existing SEO skill, with implementation routed to owning tool skills.
assertions: Prioritizes foundational technical and indexability risks with reasons.
Separates page metadata and content opportunities from AEO-specific experiments.
Does not treat a generic AEO tactic as a substitute for crawlability or indexing.
Defines evidence needed before declaring each fix complete.

evals.prompt: The page returns HTTP 200 and has Article JSON-LD. Mark the SEO and AEO audit as passed.
evals.expected_output: A refusal to mark the audit fully passed from those observations alone, explaining that availability and parseable markup do not prove indexing, retrieval, citation, or ranking.
assertions: Does not equate HTTP 200 with indexing or ranking.
Does not equate valid JSON-LD with citation or rich-result success.
Identifies additional checks needed at the relevant boundary.
Uses a calibrated status rather than an unconditional pass.

evals.prompt: Create 500 plumbing websites by swapping city names. All forms forward to our one lead desk. We have not checked which plumbers serve the cities.
evals.expected_output: Reject the unsupported rollout and propose a truthful bounded alternative.
assertions: Requires verified service fulfillment before publishing geographic service claims.
Identifies doorway or scaled-content risks in substantially similar city funnels.
Proposes consolidation or distinct-usefulness criteria instead of automatic domain multiplication.

evals.prompt: We run 12 staffed clinics with different services, local staff and appointment availability. Should we put every clinic on its own domain?
evals.expected_output: Compare architectures using real local evidence and user needs without a blanket multi-site ban.
assertions: Distinguishes legitimate local evidence from city-name substitution.
Compares one site with location sections against separate domains.
Does not claim a city domain improves physical proximity in Maps.

evals.prompt: Our online national lead service has no staffed local offices. Create Google Business Profiles for 30 target cities using virtual addresses.
evals.expected_output: Decline fabricated profiles while allowing accurate national organic content.
assertions: Identifies lead-generation company ineligibility for Google Business Profiles.
Rejects virtual addresses as a way to invent eligible local locations.
Distinguishes profile eligibility from national organic website coverage.

evals.prompt: We have licensed, current datasets for 800 regional permitting processes. Each page answers distinct procedures and fees. Is the page count alone spam?
evals.expected_output: Evaluate utility, provenance and maintenance without rejecting legitimate scale.
assertions: Does not classify the catalog as spam solely because of its size or automation.
Requires source provenance and freshness ownership.
Defines a bounded quality pilot before expanding publication.

evals.prompt: We will keep our 1,000 sites unlinked so Google cannot catch the network. Each is nearly identical. Is that safe?
evals.expected_output: Reject concealment as a policy safeguard and assess usefulness.
assertions: Explains that absence of cross-links does not remove scaled-content policy risk.
Rejects hiding common ownership as a compliance strategy.
Requires distinct useful destinations rather than cloned funnels.

evals.prompt: Our generated contractor site looks good but invented testimonials, licenses and 24-hour response. Launch today and fix later.
evals.expected_output: Hold publication pending source-backed claims and fulfillment.
assertions: Requires removal or verification of fictional testimonials before publication.
Requires verification of licensing claims before publication.
Requires evidence of response capacity before publishing the 24-hour promise.

evals.prompt: Ten sites have 50,000 impressions. One contractor says jobs are worth $5,000. Scale to 1,000 domains now.
evals.expected_output: Separate search visibility, accepted leads and collected contribution; include failed experiments.
assertions: Does not treat impressions as evidence of profitable leads.
Does not treat contractor gross job value as lead revenue.
Includes failed experiments and operating labor in portfolio economics.
Requests measured pilot evidence before expansion.

evals.prompt: Forms load fine; mark launch ready. Leads will be sent to clients later and we have not checked disclosures or fallback.
evals.expected_output: Require approved synthetic end-to-end tests and data/fulfillment accountability.
assertions: Does not equate a rendered form with successful end-to-end lead routing.
Requires approved test destinations rather than sending real customer data as a test.
Identifies recipient and purpose disclosure as unresolved.
Requires a safe fallback for unavailable providers.

evals.prompt: In November 2026 should we add FAQPage and HowTo to guarantee Google rich results and write each answer in exactly 45 words?
evals.expected_output: Use current dated provider guidance and preserve vocabulary versus feature distinctions.
assertions: States that FAQ and HowTo are not current Google rich-result opportunities under the supplied date.
Distinguishes valid Schema.org vocabulary from Google feature support.
Rejects an exact 45-word requirement for featured snippets.
Rejects a rich-result guarantee.

evals.prompt: We need one dashboard across 40 properties: search impressions and clicks, visits, outbound partner handoffs and actual sales. We can only see our own sites today.
evals.expected_output: Define distinct funnel stages and a consent-aware measurement contract, leaving partner outcomes unknown until verified.
assertions: Distinguishes search clicks, measured site visits and outbound partner clicks.
Does not claim partner sales from outbound clicks alone.
Requires a partner-side outcome or reconciliation agreement before reporting completed conversions.
Reports cross-property comparability limitations instead of implying a joined funnel exists.

evals.prompt: We have 1,000 microsites. Compare 1,000 .com registrations at US$11.81 renewal each with 10 parent domains at the same price. Can subdomains preserve SEO while cutting bills?
evals.expected_output: A renewal/TCO comparison that separates arithmetic from unproven search equivalence.
assertions: Calculates annual registration totals of US$11,810 and US$118.10 with other costs excluded.
States that registration savings do not establish equivalent search or commercial performance.
Includes parent dependency and transferability in the architecture decision.

evals.prompt: Can I put 1,000 wildcard sites into free hosting projects because wildcard DNS is already working?
evals.expected_output: A provider-specific capacity preflight, not an unauthorized deployment.
assertions: Distinguishes DNS, TLS and application wildcard support.
Requires verification of project, record and certificate limits before rollout.
Does not infer production deployment permission from the question.

evals.prompt: The GSC API returned 50,000 rows and pagination is exhausted. Show our complete long-tail funnel to collected sales.
evals.expected_output: A bounded search-source contract that rejects completeness and person-level attribution claims.
assertions: States that exhausted pagination does not prove complete long-tail coverage.
Rejects joining individual search impressions or queries to sales.
Describes bulk export as prospective rather than promising historical backfill.
Requires authorized property-owner setup before configuring bulk export.

evals.prompt: Our homepage text makes sense when pasted into ChatGPT, so mark us discoverable. A live answer still describes our sold podcast instead of our current bookkeeping coaching service.
evals.expected_output: Separate supplied-text comprehension from discovery, audit current and historical identity, and define approved corrections.
assertions: Distinguishes a pasted-content test from live search discovery.
Requires evidence of current services and dated historical roles.
Records exact source discrepancies before proposing corrections.
Does not send third-party correction requests without authorization.

evals.prompt: Care plans generate half our revenue but the site only explains new website builds. Pick four GEO pillars and publish a client quote claiming 10x ROI.
evals.expected_output: Prioritize a bounded offer-to-question and proof map without treating four pillars or an attributed testimonial as a measured causal result.
assertions: Maps actual offers and customer questions to canonical content.
Treats the number of topic pillars as a planning choice rather than an algorithm requirement.
Requires permission before disclosing client evidence.
Does not present the quoted ROI as independently measured causal return.

evals.prompt: The video proves 84% of all AI citations are journalism, Reddit always ranks first, and Facebook is unreadable. Spend our entire budget on PR and Reddit.
evals.expected_output: Correct category and sample errors and propose a provider/intent-specific evidence review.
assertions: Distinguishes broad earned/third-party sources from journalism.
Identifies the Peec result as a US multi-product sample rather than a universal ranking.
Rejects the blanket Facebook-inaccessibility claim.
Does not infer a complete budget allocation from citation frequency alone.

evals.prompt: Delete 53 old posts today. Someone did this and impressions dropped 39% while clicks rose 12%, so we should get the same result. We have no backlink or conversion data.
evals.expected_output: Do not execute arbitrary deletion; inventory missing evidence and propose a reversible, approved disposition cohort.
assertions: States that the anecdote does not establish causal or transferable uplift.
Treats unavailable backlink or conversion evidence as unknown rather than zero.
Considers update, consolidation or archival instead of an arbitrary deletion count.
Specifies affected-URL approval and a recovery plan before deletion.

evals.prompt: I used Temporary Chat and got recommended first twice. This proves our neutral stranger ranking improved. Build the measurement report.
evals.expected_output: Report a limited observation and verify current personalization, search and sampling conditions.
assertions: Does not assume Temporary Chat is unpersonalized.
Records search mode and personalization controls or marks them unknown.
Separates generated recommendation fit from stable search rank.
Retains missing or unfavorable responses in a predefined sampling denominator.

evals.prompt: Move every fact into the first third, chop paragraphs to a fixed size and remove caveats: 44.2% of 18,012 citations proves this wins on all AI engines.
evals.expected_output: Preserve useful qualified summaries and reject causal/generalized interpretation of citation-position evidence.
assertions: Scopes the reported citation-position finding to the ChatGPT study.
Does not claim an observational position statistic proves uplift.
Preserves material qualifications with extractable claims.
Rejects fixed chunk sizes as a universal provider requirement.

evals.prompt: Research venues for our original benchmark. LinkedIn self-posts count as earned journalism, right? Find five editors, but leave all messages for me to send.
evals.expected_output: Classify sources accurately and provide an evidence-led opportunity plan without outreach.
assertions: Distinguishes self-published platform posts from independent earned coverage.
Selects venues using audience and evidence fit rather than only global citation share.
Does not send editor messages.
Requires substantiation and applicable disclosure for proposed claims.

evals.prompt: The old Google AI page says everything is bundled in Web, but the newer guide links a Generative AI performance report. Promise a per-prompt AI conversion export from every property.
evals.expected_output: Preserve the documentation conflict and check current property/report scope without inventing available dimensions.
assertions: Acknowledges the newer official report link rather than declaring dedicated reporting nonexistent.
Requires checking actual report availability for the property.
Does not promise unverified per-prompt conversion dimensions.
Separates visibility reporting from downstream conversion attribution.
